laat_vaar.blok: Wat die stasie met die steenkool doen
laat_vaar.voor: kook water in sterk pype tot stoom
laat_vaar.na: kook water in sterk pype totdat dit stoom word
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Water tot stoom kook' is a compressed, wooden construction; 'totdat dit stoom word' is the natural Afrikaans way to say the water boils until it becomes steam.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Water tot stoom kook' is a normal Afrikaans resultative (like 'tot moes kook'), so the proposal is a longer lateral move and adds an ambiguous 'dit'.

laat_vaar.blok: Nie elke stasie brand steenkool nie
laat_vaar.voor: kook ook water tot stoom wat 'n masjien laat draai
laat_vaar.na: kook ook water totdat dit stoom word, en die stoom laat 'n masjien draai
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Same wooden 'kook tot stoom' construction as earlier in the lesson; splitting it into two clauses (with the AWS comma) also removes the ambiguous 'wat' that could refer to the water.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The 'wat' attaches naturally to the nearest noun, 'stoom', so it is not ambiguous; splitting the sentence makes it longer without making it clearly better, and it stays consistent with the first sentence, which was also left alone.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: A definition opening with a bare 'Dit' reads stiffly; 'Die ding waaruit' is clearer for Grade 5 and matches the lesson's own sentence 'Die bron is die ding waaruit die stasie sy energie kry'.
na_skrywer.fout: The definition opens with a bare 'Dit' and ends with 'waarmee dit werk', so two uses of 'dit' point to different things (the source and the power station), which a Grade 5 reader can stumble over.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a real but small stiffness in a glossary definition, and the wording beyond a plain spelling or grammar error belongs to the writer.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: ver genoeg terug en jy kom
laat_vaar_vorige.na: ver genoeg terug, en jy kom
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two complete sentences here (an imperative and 'jy kom ... uit'), so a comma goes before it.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The first clause is an imperative with no subject of its own and the sentence is one tight 'do this and you get that' unit, so the house comma rule does not require a comma.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As a conjunction introducing a clause, standard written Afrikaans uses 'totdat' rather than 'tot'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot' is standard Afrikaans as a conjunction, so 'totdat' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat die stasie met die steenkool doen
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In written study text a thing (the machine) is referred to as 'dit', not the colloquial 'hom'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'hom' points unambiguously to the machine, whereas 'dit' could also point back to 'die stoom' in the same sentence.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Nie elke stasie brand steenkool nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: This is the first machine mentioned at the dam station, so the indefinite article fits, as in the block's last sentence and the glossary.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'die masjien' reads naturally as the turning machine the reader has already met, so the article swap is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: loop nie langs net een draad nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: loop nie net langs een draad nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans 'net' naturally stands before the preposition phrase it limits, so 'nie net langs een draad nie' reads more naturally; meaning unchanged.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original 'langs net een draad' reads naturally and says exactly 'along only one wire'; moving 'net' in front of 'langs' turns it towards 'nie net ... nie' ('not merely along a wire'), a particle shift that loosens the meaning without fixing a fault.
